sources.title: View the communication panel for conversations

notes.title: Separate chat routing from widget rollout
notes.body:
Start by choosing Messaging and Chat for the workstream. It owns routing and assignment behavior; the widget is the customer-facing entry point. Multiple chat channels may share that workstream, so plan shared routing deliberately.

For an existing classic channel, adding Modern UI preserves the workstream configuration. Test with the version-specific testing script. The general script follows whichever version is active, so changing that selection is a release decision, not just a preview action. Confirm the intended version on a test page before switching the live channel.

notes.title: Plan proactive invitations around customer choice
notes.body:
For Contact Center standalone, first enable proactive chat on the widget and ensure the target page embeds it. The visitor receives an invitation and can decline it; the representative notification follows acceptance.

Choose a meaningful trigger separately from the invitation wording. The developer example uses elapsed time after widget readiness. Supply the message through notificationUIConfig and choose showPrechat intentionally if the widget has a survey. Test the accept and decline paths as well as the trigger itself; an invitation is not an already accepted service conversation.

notes.title: Publish quick replies for the right audience
notes.body:
Treat language and audience as separate checks. Write a separate response for each locale; selecting a locale does not translate its text. Associate departmental replies with the relevant workstreams. A reply without an association is broadly available, subject to language settings.

Then check the representative experience. Administrator-created responses appear on All, while personal responses appear on Personal when that feature is enabled. Before duplicating an apparently missing response, check the tab, language and workstream. This keeps a useful shared response from becoming several separately maintained personal copies.

cards.prompt: Which workstream type and channel should you select for live chat?
cards.answer: Messaging type with Chat as the channel.
cards.explanation: The workstream controls how those conversations are routed and assigned.

cards.prompt: Which widget script should a test page use to stay on one chosen version even when the active version changes?
cards.explanation: The general script follows the active version instead.

cards.prompt: Two websites need different chat presentation but must share one maintained routing and assignment configuration. Which design fits that requirement?
cards.answer: Use separate chat channels attached to one shared workstream.
cards.explanation: Channels of the same type can share a workstream. Separate workstreams introduce separate routing maintenance; changing queues or channel types is not the requested separation.

options.text: Create separate workstreams and manually copy every routing update.
Use separate chat channels attached to one shared workstream.
Use one widget and change the queue whenever visitors change websites.
Use two channel types under one workstream to separate the branding.

cards.prompt: In standalone Contact Center proactive chat, what customer action causes a representative to receive the chat notification?
cards.explanation: Showing the invitation alone does not mean that the customer accepted a conversation.

cards.prompt: For startProactiveChat, which argument controls whether the widget's configured prechat survey is displayed?
cards.explanation: It is a Boolean argument; it controls that invitation flow rather than deleting the survey configuration.

cards.prompt: A standalone website already triggers proactive chat at the intended moment. The invitation should explain why help is offered on that page, while preserving its survey. What should the developer change?
cards.answer: Pass the invitation message in notificationUIConfig.
cards.explanation: The API separates invitation text from survey visibility. Representative notification templates and fallback routing address different parts of the service flow.

options.text: Pass the invitation message in notificationUIConfig.
Set showPrechat to false without changing the message configuration.

cards.prompt: What is the workstream scope of an administrator quick reply with no workstream association?
cards.answer: It is available across workstreams rather than restricted to one.
cards.explanation: Language settings still affect which replies a representative sees.

cards.prompt: Does selecting a quick reply's locale translate its message into that language?
cards.answer: No. Author a separate translated reply for each required locale.
cards.explanation: Locale identifies the reply's language; it does not generate translated text.

cards.prompt: An administrator has published an approved response in the correct language and workstream. A representative is looking for it on Personal. What is the most direct next step?
cards.answer: Open All in the Quick replies panel.
cards.explanation: Administrator responses are on All. A new personal copy or broader audience would change content management unnecessarily; the scenario already establishes the correct language.

options.text: Create a personal duplicate of the approved response.
Remove its workstream association to make it global.
Open All in the Quick replies panel.
